title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1LA0RE_0LD0LB_1RA1LD_0RC1RF_0RA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1LA0RE_0LD0LB_1RA1LD_0RC1RF_0RA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 84,949 cells have been visited and 45,874 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.603).

claims.title: Macro structure (observed)
claims.text: A nested bouncer: a reservoir (010)^n at the right is consumed about 6 per pass while units U = (010)^17 (100)^16 1 are emitted at the left; when it is empty the next level, made of units V = (010)^55 (100)^54 1, takes over; three or more levels seen.

claims.title: No halt in the first 6.88×10<sup>16</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 6.88×1016 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.22×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 1,528 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The decider pipeline of bbchallenge left it open; no proof either way is recorded here yet.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LC_1LA0RD_0LD1LF_0RE0RA_1LB1RE_0LB--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1LA_1RC0LD_1LB0RE_0LA0LC_0RD1RF_0RB--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 84,949 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.22×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: Units within units
html: The tape is built from units. At level 1 the unit is (010)^17 (100)^16 1; at level 2 (010)^55 (100)^54 1. The head eats a reservoir of (010) words at the right end and emits one level-1 unit at the left every few passes; when the reservoir is gone, the next level reorganises and a new reservoir appears. The units grow about three times per level.

This is read off long runs, not yet proved: the next step is to state these patterns as rules, prove them with tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py, and see whether the counters can ever reach the configuration that halts.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.603).
After 109 steps the tape spans 84,949 cells (2,283 left of the start, 62,592 right), with a density of 1s of 0.54.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
